opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee he is eligible for write (up to write; admin only if role owns the system, which applies here but write was requested). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E031 (Nathaniel Young) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested write > max, so recommend read. (Note: this conflicts with the earlier note listing full-time.)
reason: The two team notes conflict on employment type: HR reports E031 as full-time Payroll Specialist (eligible up to write, and admin since the role owns Payroll), while Security reports E031 as a contractor with basic security training (eligible only for read, since write requires advanced training and contractors never get admin). Because the evidence conflicts and under the security-reported facts a write would exceed the permitted maximum, I grant the most restrictive level consistent with all available information: read.
